# generator-shortcuts

The strongest plausible shortcut I found is:

> Reflect source cells only when they are on the lower-coordinate side of the
> painted axis: left of a vertical axis or above a horizontal axis. Otherwise
> leave the grid unchanged.

This rival fits all three usable canonical pairs. Each canonical input places
its source on the left of a vertical color-5 line or above a horizontal one, so
the demonstrations never require reflection from right to left or bottom to
top. The original generator reinforced the same shortcut because it emitted
only a centered vertical axis with a left-side monochrome blob.

An exact disagreement is retained at
`repo/generators/250671db7aa1/counterexamples/after_side.json`:

```json
[
  [0,0,0,5,0,0,0],
  [0,0,0,5,0,0,0],
  [0,0,0,5,2,2,0],
  [0,0,0,5,0,2,0],
  [0,0,0,5,0,0,0],
  [0,0,0,5,0,0,0],
  [0,0,0,5,0,0,0]
]
```

The intended rule mirrors the three color-2 cells from the right side of column
3 onto `(2,2)`, `(2,1)`, and `(3,1)`, preserving the originals. The shortcut
sees no lower-coordinate-side source and returns the input unchanged.

I checked the intended output with the supported canonical Racket command. The
source-bound result is in
`checks/counterexample-250671db7aa1/racket.json`; it executed rule hash
`27bdc557ee50`, generator SHA-256
`b35b37b2cd0d12dc204c06dc40b490f1b1f329af2700b7141b488021f48a4cae`,
and exactly matched the retained expected output. The focused regression test
also directly compares the declared shortcut against that output.

The repaired generator **does emit such cases by default**. Schedule slots 2
and 3 of every four-sample cycle place sources after the axis, in vertical and
horizontal orientations respectively. More strongly, each five-pair lesson
window supplies four demonstrations after any single query holdout; the full
300-lesson census checked all **1,500/1,500 query rotations** with zero surviving
declared-rival ambiguity. The fixed-period census checked all 12 cyclic
start/band combinations and **60/60 rotations**.
